flags.text: The stem prints K_c and K_p with underscores (the player typesets them) and hands over the formula and dn = -1, so the item tests arithmetic more than the idea. Suggested wording for Thomas to review (not applied): "For 2 NO2(g) <=> N2O4(g) at 298 K, Kc = 4.7. What is Kp?" Key unchanged.

Concept-first rule: dividing by 0.0821 x 298 is calculator work in a no-calculator section, and 0.0085 and 41 have no single-slip route (the notes say so). A lighter variant asks whether Kp is above or below Kc, or gives RT as about 25. Key unchanged.
The stem value Kc = 4.7 M^-1 is a made-up number (the measured dimerization constant at 298 K is about 200 M^-1). Fine as an exercise; the explainer never calls it the real value.
The Kc / Kp module has a Q-against-K slider but no Kc to Kp converter. A dn and RT slider would make this the exact play-with state.

served.stem: For the gas-phase equilibrium 2 NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g) at 298 K, the equilibrium constant in terms of concentrations is K_c = 4.7 M⁻¹. Using K_p = K_c·(RT)^Δn with R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K and Δn = (1 − 2) = -1, calculate K_p at 298 K.
served.bankWhy: Δn = mol gas products - mol gas reactants = 1 - 2 = -1. K_p = K_c·(RT)^Δn = 4.7 × (0.0821 × 298)^(-1) = 4.7 / 24.5 ≈ 0.19. Negative Δn means K_p < K_c whenever RT > 1, as it always is at room temperature.

answer.line: Gas moles drop from 2 to 1, so dn = -1 and you divide K_c by RT. 4.7 over about 24.5 is 0.19.

steps: Count gas moles first. Two NO2 on the left, one N2O4 on the right: dn = 1 - 2 = -1.
Know what dn = -1 does. K_p = K_c x (RT)^-1, so you divide by RT once. Fewer gas moles on the product side puts K_p below K_c.
Estimate RT: 0.0821 x 298 is about 24.5. Then 4.7 / 24.5 is a little under 0.2: 0.19.

choices.note: Dividing by RT twice gives about 0.008, the nearest route to this choice. dn = -1 means one division, not two.
One division by RT for one mole of gas lost.
K_p equals K_c only when dn = 0. Here the gas moles drop by one, so the RT factor is real.
No one slip turns 4.7 into 41. It sits above K_c, and losing gas moles means K_p has to land below K_c.
4.7 x 24.5 = 115 is what dn = +1 would give. The minus sign on dn means divide by RT.

student.lockIt: K_p = K_c (RT)^dn. Fewer gas moles on the product side puts K_p below K_c.
